svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop
svg.desc: A self-contained educational SVG interface showing a detailed flower anatomy diagram, ten empty label targets, a word bank, instructions, a pollination inset, and anchor-driven Hint, Check Answer, and Reset popup panels.

g.text: Match each term from the word bank to the correct structure on the flower.
Use the arrows and visible structures to decide where each word belongs.
Dashed boxes are target areas; arrows identify the structure to label.
Study shape, position, and biological function.
Pick a tile from the word bank below.
Follow an arrow to its empty label slot.
Use Hint or Check Answer when ready.
Pollen moves from anther to stigma.
Fertilization can produce seeds in the ovary.
Select the term that best matches each numbered arrow.
Static SVG learning interface · no JavaScript or external assets
Look for visual clues before opening the full answer key.

g.text: Male structure: stamen = anther + filament. Female structure: pistil = stigma + style + ovary.
Compare each numbered target with the matching flower structure.
Pollen-producing part at a stamen’s tip.
Leaflike part protecting the developing bud.
Base where the flower’s organs attach.
Female organ: stigma, style, and ovary.
Male organ formed by anther and filament.
Say each organ’s function aloud to strengthen recall.
The learning screen is ready to begin again.
Returning closes all popup layers and restores the clean activity view.
